reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern exhibits a robust quasi-periodic cadence of ~98 points per cycle, consistent with the estimated period. Each cycle contains one dominant sharp positive spike (peak amplitude 3–5 robust std units) followed by a rapid decay and a shallow, noisy trough region. Baseline levels hover near zero (median within ±0.16), with mild drifts (slope per point ≈ ±0.002–0.011) that are non-systematic across candidates. Peaks are asymmetric: steep rise (~5–10 points), slower fall (~15–25 points), often with a small secondary hump on the descent. Troughs are irregular, low-amplitude (−1 to 0), and frequently contain small oscillations or flat segments. Noise is moderate (MAD 0.49–0.72), appearing as fine-grained jitter superimposed on the main motif; roughness values (0.11–0.13) confirm low-to-moderate irregularity. Amplitude variability is acceptable: 90th-percentile amplitude ranges from 3.28 to 5.03, reflecting natural scaling with window length and local variance. No candidate shows sustained monotonic trends or persistent outliers beyond single-cycle spikes. Boundary truncation is minimal; all windows capture full cycles without cutting peaks mid-rise/fall. Acceptable variation includes slight differences in peak sharpness, trough depth, and inter-peak spacing (±5–10 points), but the core motif—single sharp spike per ~98-point segment—is highly conserved.

reference_profiles.description: Short 1-cycle window (98 pts); shows one clear spike at ~40–43, preceded by modest fluctuations and followed by a dip to −1. Baseline near −0.11; noise is relatively low (MAD 0.49), roughness low (0.115). Peak is sharp, symmetric-ish rise/fall, no secondary humps. Ends cleanly before next cycle begins.

3-cycle window (294 pts); contains three well-separated spikes at ~930, 1025, 1120. Each spike has steep rise, plateau-like top, and asymmetric decay. Baseline drifts slightly upward (slope +0.0023). One flat segment (~950–965) suggests possible artifact or transient stabilization, but overall morphology matches consensus. Slightly higher MAD (0.69) reflects more noise in trough regions.

3-cycle window (294 pts); spikes at ~1750, 1845, 1940. Similar spike shape to ref 1, but second spike shows a small secondary hump on descent. Baseline drifts upward more noticeably (slope +0.011), yet remains within expected variation; median −0.062. Troughs are slightly deeper and noisier. Amplitude_90 highest among 3P windows (4.14), indicating locally elevated variance but not anomalous structure.

5-cycle window (490 pts); five spikes spaced ~98 pts apart, confirming periodicity. Spikes are taller (amplitude_90 = 5.03) and slightly broader; some show double-peaked tops (e.g., ~2550, 2740). Baseline near zero, very slight negative drift (slope −0.001). Highest roughness (0.132) due to denser fine structure in troughs, but no sustained deviations. Best for assessing long-term stability and inter-cycle consistency.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 0 for queries with single-cycle length or ambiguous periodicity—it provides the clearest isolated motif. Use reference 1 for queries with 2–3 cycles where baseline stability and spike symmetry are key. Reference 2 is best when queries show mild upward drift or secondary hump features; treat its higher slope as acceptable variation. Reference 3 is optimal for longer queries (>400 pts) or when assessing multi-cycle coherence, especially if spikes appear broader or double-peaked. Avoid overfitting to ref 2’s drift; consensus across refs 0,1,3 confirms drift is not structural.
uncertainties: Whether the flat segment in ref 1 is intrinsic behavior or a localized artifact
Exact tolerance for secondary humps on spikes (present in ref 2 & 3, absent in ref 0)
Whether amplitude scaling with window length is purely statistical or reflects true signal dynamics
No ground-truth labels prevent quantifying contamination risk beyond cross-consistency

subtask_history.goal: Inspect a global overview and characterize the dominant pattern and deviations.
subtask_history.summary: A global overview of [0, 5304] reveals a dominant quasi-periodic spike-trough motif (~98 pts/cycle), with baseline near 0 (±0.16), moderate noise (MAD ~0.5–0.7), and characteristic sharp spikes (rise: 5–10 pts; decay: 15–25 pts). Three high-confidence anomalies were identified: (i) a flat segment at [1395,1405] (y≈−1, 10 pts, confidence 0.87), inconsistent with reference troughs and coinciding with expected spike timing—suggesting missing spike + stabilization; (ii) attenuated spikes at [2790,2820] (3 cycles, amplitude ≤2.5 vs typical ≥3.28, confidence 0.78), indicating localized suppression; (iii) a sustained dip at [4745,4775] (30 pts, median −1.2, no compensating spike, confidence 0.92), violating the one-spike-per-cycle rule and exceeding allowable drift. No further non-redundant evidence actions remain; the sub-task is complete with unresolved uncertainty only regarding root cause (e.g., sensor stall vs filtering artifact) for anomalies (i) and (ii).
